question.prompt:
Toothpicks of equal length are used to build a rectangular grid as shown. If the grid is \(20\) toothpicks high and \(10\) toothpicks wide, then the number of toothpicks used is

[Figure 1](figures/1989_AMC_12_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Separate the toothpicks into horizontal and vertical groups. This lets us count each shared side of neighboring squares just once.

The grid is \(20\) squares high, so there are \(21\) horizontal lines: one at each boundary between rows, plus the top and bottom boundaries. Each horizontal line contains \(10\) toothpicks. Similarly, the \(10\) columns of squares have \(11\) vertical boundary lines, each containing \(20\) toothpicks. Therefore the total is
\[
21\cdot10+11\cdot20=210+220=430.
\]
Every toothpick belongs to exactly one horizontal or vertical line, so the count includes all toothpicks without repetition. The answer is \(\boxed{430}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
solutions.title: Count toothpicks by direction
